comment: Mutation testing for the DOCUMENTATION PIPELINE. A SECOND config rather than entries in stryker-config.json because Stryker mutates one 'project' per run. This library exists as a non-test project precisely so it can be mutated: Stryker treats test projects as the test-projects, so a renderer living in DwarfMapper.Generator.Tests could never be a mutation target, and nothing would prove the doc tests catch a defect in the renderer itself. Run via scripts/housekeeping.ps1 -Mutation, and nightly in CI via the 'mutation' matrix job (leg: doctooling) in .github/workflows/ci.yml (needs: dotnet tool install -g dotnet-stryker --version 4.16.0). RE-MEASURED 2026-08-21 on Stryker 4.16.0 after the H7 phase-2 hang elimination (progress guard in DocSnippetInjector.Inject; Dedent's trim loops restructured to FindIndex/FindLastIndex/GetRange), against the WHOLE test suite (4,789 tests discovered), 12 logical cores: score 67.96 % (193 detected of 284 scoreable — 193 killed + 0 timeout; 54 survived, 37 uncovered, 67 compile errors excluded, 7 guard mutants Ignored via in-source Stryker disable), 5 min 04 s wall-clock. break is that score floored to 67. The 2026-08-19 post-T3-H1 measurement was the same 67.96 % as 191 killed + 2 timeout of the same 284 scoreable — phase 2 turned the two genuine hangs into ordinary sub-second kills without moving the score. THE EARLIER 83.10 % (236/284, 2026-08-19 pre-guard) WAS INFLATED BY THE T3-H1 DEFECT ITSELF: with write-back live, the first destructive mutant emptied the committed documents on the REAL tree, and every later mutant session then compared its renderer output against that polluted committed text — 43 mutants were 'killed' by the destruction, not by any assertion about their own behaviour. All 43 are no-ops on the current documentation corpus and survive on a stable tree: real corpus holes, exposed (not created) by the guard, catalogued under 'T3-H1 fix' in Issues/ledgers/T3-mutation-survivors.md. The mutant space is IDENTICAL across the two runs (284 scoreable both times; the only flips are those 43 plus one Timeout that became a clean Kill), so 67 is the leg's first HONEST floor, not a regression. Historical: before 2026-08-16 the config could not run at all ('comment' sat inside 'stryker-config', which Stryker 4.16 rejects) and its 'mutate' globs were repo-root-relative, producing a VACUOUS run that still exits 0; the inherited break of 70 had never been measured. NOTE 1 — THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO 'additional-timeout' HERE, AND SINCE H7 PHASE 2 (2026-08-21) THE LEG HAS ZERO TIMEOUT-CLASSIFIED MUTANTS — the default per-mutant ceiling is a pure backstop no mutant is expected to reach. History: this leg carried the project's only three GENUINE hangs. SnippetScanner.cs Dedent deleting 'kept.RemoveAt(...)' in either blank-line trim loop froze the loop state into an unconditional, side-effect-free infinite spin — only the wall clock could end it, so both classified Timeout stably in every run. DocSnippetInjector.cs deleting the prose branch's 'i++' pinned the loop on one line, re-appending it to the result StringBuilder forever — that runaway ALLOCATES, so it terminated itself by memory exhaustion (~4 GB) on the same order as the per-mutant ceiling, and its classification was a race: Timeout in the 2026-08-19.07-03 run, Killed in the 11-49 run, same day, same suite. (An earlier version of this note claimed the post-guard kill happened 'outright before the loop is reached' — VERIFIED FALSE: both killing tests inject real prose-first documents, the loop IS reached, and the kill was the OOM inside the runaway loop racing the clock. Full dissection: Issues/ledgers/H7-timeout-dissection.md.) H7 phase 2 removed the hang class structurally: Dedent's mutable trim loops became FindIndex/FindLastIndex/GetRange (behaviour-identical incl. the empty-region throw; any mutation there now yields a wrong slice or an immediate ArgumentException, killed in microseconds by SnippetScannerTests.Leading_and_trailing_blank_lines_are_trimmed_from_the_region), and Inject's loop carries a progress guard ('i <= previous' throws InvalidOperationException naming file and line; the guard sits in a 'Stryker disable all' block — its 7 mutants report Ignored, correct because the guard is reachable only when the loop body is already defective). The 'i++'-deletion mutant now dies deterministically in microseconds via the guard (verified 2026-08-21: 193 Killed, 0 Timeout). IF a Timeout ever appears here again it is by definition a clock artifact on a mutant that cannot hang — raise 'additional-timeout' as the siblings do; never filter the test set. NOTE 2 — WHY THIS LEG IS FAST AND ITS SIBLING IS NOT: ZERO of its 284 scoreable mutants are 'static', so Stryker attributes per-test coverage to every one of them and the covering sets are tiny (1,603 test executions in total). The generator leg has 85 static mutants, each of which re-runs the entire suite, and it costs 21 minutes. The difference is coverage attribution, not test quality. NOTE 3 — THIS LEG USED TO REWRITE TRACKED DOCUMENTATION, AND THE MECHANISM IS GUARDED SINCE 2026-08-19 (T3-H1). The doc-generation tests heal-or-fail into README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/diagnostics.md, docs/options.md and samples/DwarfMapper.Gallery/README.md, and the mutants under test are the code that writes them; the first completed run left three of those files EMPTIED (2,523 deleted lines across five files, reverted). The verified mechanism: Stryker 4.16 has NO sandbox for test execution — it swaps the mutated assembly into each test project's REAL bin folder in place (leaving 'X.dll.stryker-unchanged' beside it), so AppContext.BaseDirectory is the real bin, every repo-root walk resolves the real repository, and a mutated renderer wrote its output over the real files. The guard is RepoWriteGuard (tests/DwarfMapper.Generator.Tests/Contracts — deliberately in the TEST project, because a guard inside this mutation target could itself be mutated off): every test-side repo write routes through it, and it REFUSES the write when it detects a mutation run ('*.stryker-unchanged' beside the test assembly, or a 'StrykerOutput'/'.stryker-tmp' ancestor). NO TEST IS EXCLUDED from this leg and every staleness assertion still runs and still fails — only the write-back is suppressed — so the kills are unchanged; a post-run 'git status' is expected CLEAN, and RepoWriteGuardTests pins both the detection and the refusal. The pre-guard MutantControl pollution history is in Issues/ledgers/E3-E1-report.md, the fix measurement in Issues/ledgers/T3-mutation-survivors.md under 'T3-H1 fix'. NOTE 4 — the 'mutate' globs must be PROJECT-relative ('**/Name.cs'), never repo-root-relative: Stryker resolves them against src/DwarfMapper.DocTooling, so a repo-root path matches nothing, every mutant is dropped with 'Removed by mutate filter', and Stryker STILL EXITS 0. Assert-MutantsWereTested (scripts/housekeeping.ps1) exists for exactly that hazard; it counts scoreable statuses in the JSON report and returns 284 for this run. NOTE 5 — Stryker mutates and COMPILES the whole project regardless of these globs (567 mutants created; 183 dropped by the mutate filter; 67 rolled back as compile errors; 26 dropped by the block-already-covered filter; 7 Ignored by the progress guard's in-source Stryker disable; 247 tested plus 37 uncovered), and only then filters what is TESTED. The report therefore contains every file in the project; the five named here are the only ones carrying scoreable statuses, and that is the non-vacuity check to make. NOTE 6 — there is deliberately NO 'test-projects' key. It would be INERT: Stryker discovers the solution and enumerates EVERY test project in it, so such a list does not select the test set; see NOTE 3 in stryker-config.runtime.json for the measurement that established this. It was removed rather than corrected, so nothing here pretends to scope anything. NOTE 7 — THE MARGIN TO break IS THREE MUTANTS. 193/284 is 67.96 %; 190/284 is 66.90 % and FAILS. break is the floored measured score, as in all three configs. Since H7 phase 2 all 193 detections are ordinary Kills — no part of the score rides on a Timeout classification any more, so the score is no longer load-sensitive: a run landing under 67 is a real regression (or a mutant-population shift from a product edit), not scheduler noise. NOTE 8 — the original 11 survivors and 37 uncovered mutants are catalogued, with a real-hole-or-equivalent judgement for each, in Issues/ledgers/T3-mutation-survivors.md; the 43 additional survivors the T3-H1 guard exposed (pollution kills reclassified as the corpus holes they always were) are recorded there under 'T3-H1 fix'. Raise break only by killing survivors. NOTE 9 — 'low' MUST STAY >= 'break' or Stryker 4.16 REFUSES TO RUN AT ALL ('Threshold low must be more than or equal to threshold break') — and refuses with EXIT CODE 0, so nothing downstream notices except Assert-MutantsWereTested. T3 raised break from 70 to 83 but left low at 80, which made this leg unrunnable from 2026-08-19 until the T3-H1 fix re-ran it; low now tracks break (a report-colouring threshold, not a ratchet). Whenever break moves, move low with it. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-22 (round-22 P3, same Stryker 4.16.0, whole suite — 4,846 tests discovered, quiet machine, StrykerOutput/2026-08-21.23-56-18): score 95.42 % (271 killed of 284 scoreable; 13 survived, 0 uncovered, 0 timeouts, 67 compile errors excluded, 7 guard mutants Ignored), 4 min 36 s wall-clock, so break moves 67 -> 95 (95.42 floored), low with it, and high 90 -> 96 to stay above low. The rise is the P3 kill program landing: T3's families A-D + ParseId (DocTableInjector and OptionTableRenderer gained dedicated test files; ExampleCatalogue.Build's refusals are reached through the internal file-list seam; every Assert.Throws<DocToolingException> across the doc-pipeline tests now pins a discriminating message fragment AND the reported file:line) plus 38 of the 43 write-back-exposed corpus holes. THE THIRTEEN REMAINING UNDETECTED MUTANTS ARE ALL DISPOSITIONED, none chaseable with an honest test: ten are proven-equivalent ledger entries (Issues/ledgers/equivalent-mutants.md — the long-standing LongestBacktickRun boundary plus nine adjudicated in P3, including two provable only from Stryker's own mechanics: the TryCreate catch-block removal falls through to Stryker's injected 'return default', which IS null, and the Format(string) conditional-false always takes an arm that renders the identical text for the empty string), and three are filesystem-composition-root corpus holes (ScanAll's OrderBy and '*.cs' filter, ExampleCatalogue.Scan's '*.cs' filter) reachable only by planting files in the real samples/ tree or redirecting RepoLayout — both banned; they stay named survivors in the T3 ledger's P3 section and TASKS.md I2. NOTE 7's three-mutant margin described the 67-era floor and is superseded: the margin is now TWO FLIPS (270/284 = 95.07 % still passes at 95; 269/284 = 94.71 % fails), and with every undetected mutant dispositioned, a run under 95 is a real regression or a mutant-population shift from a product edit — never an undispositioned leftover.
